findings.title: Description issues instructions to the model
findings.detail: Description of "larp_check" contains imperative instructions directed at the AI assistant rather than describing the tool. This is the core tool-poisoning technique.

evidence.snippet: LARP check: is there a real product behind a coin on Robinhood Chain or Solana? Toll reads the coin's own site, launch post and code README, lists each thing it…

findings.remediation: Treat the server as untrusted; the model may obey embedded instructions.

findings.title: Description uses pressure/override language
findings.detail: Description of "larp_check" stacks urgency/override words (always, never). Legitimate tool descriptions rarely pressure the model to act or ignore prior guidance.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: larp_check · Private data: check_coin, dev_record, wallet_privacy, fresh_launches, launch_record · Public sink: larp_check.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: larp_check · Private data: check_coin, dev_record, wallet_privacy, fresh_launches, launch_record · Public sink: larp_check

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
